name: Dataset Profiler
description: Container tool that profiles any tabular dataset (CSV, TSV, or JSON) into an HTML or PDF report. Concatenates the inputs, identifies numeric (non-boolean) columns, renders per-column distribution histograms or a sample x metric heatmap, and emits a Jinja-templated report — PDF rendering via WeasyPrint. Works standalone on an uploaded file or inside a pipeline on upstream artifacts.

input_schema.title: dataset-profiler inputs
input_schema.description: Tabular data to summarise. The single `dataset` field is the standalone upload (resolved by the worker to inputs['dataset_file']). In a pipeline this field is left empty: the orchestrator injects upstream step artifacts under inputs['upstream'] / inputs['upstream_csvs'] from the step's `depends_on`, so no input field is needed for them.

dataset.description: A tabular/structured data file (CSV, TSV, or JSON) to summarise. Uploaded/pasted/selected by the user; the worker hands the tool the resolved path as `dataset_file`.

output_schema.title: dataset-profiler result
output_schema.description: Dict returned by run(...) and written to /work/output/result.json by the runtime. Side-effect artifacts (report.{pdf,html}, plot_*.png) are written under /work/output/ as well.

report_file.description: Filename of the rendered report under /work/output/

n_rows.description: Total rows across all concatenated input tables

numeric_columns.description: Numeric (non-boolean, non-identifier) columns that were plotted

plots.description: Histogram plot filenames (empty when include_plots is false)

include_plots.description: Render per-column distribution histograms and embed them in the report.

title.description: Report title shown on the cover page.

input_format.description: Force a reader for the input tables. `auto` infers from each file's extension; set csv/tsv/json when extensions are missing or misleading.

plot_type.description: `histogram` shows each numeric column's distribution. `heatmap` renders a single rows=samples x cols=numeric heatmap, rows labelled by the first non-numeric column (e.g. an id) and each column normalised independently; it falls back to histograms when the table has more than 50 rows.
